title: Samsung Plans Second Texas Chip Fab in $37 Billion Expansion
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Samsung Electronics plans to build a second semiconductor factory in Taylor, Texas, as part of a broader Central Texas investment exceeding $37 billion. The company has targeted late 2026 for construction to begin and 2030 for mass production at the new facility, known as Taylor Fab 2. It will sit next to Samsung’s first Taylor factory, where the company plans to expand production capacity for its 2-nanometer process as operations ramp up.

The investment covers both Taylor logic factories, a research and development fabrication facility, and an expansion of Samsung’s existing Austin operations. In December 2024, the U.S. Commerce Department awarded Samsung up to $4.745 billion in direct funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. Federal estimates put job creation across the program at more than 3,500 manufacturing positions and 12,000 construction jobs.

The second factory could also help Samsung supply a critical component for AI accelerators. Reuters, citing South Korea’s Maeil Business Newspaper, reported that Samsung would use Taylor Fab 2 to make base dies for high-bandwidth memory intended for AMD and Nvidia. A base die sits beneath the stacked memory dies and provides the interface through which the stack communicates with the accelerator. Samsung separately reported growth in sales of high-bandwidth memory base dies in its third-quarter results.

The Texas sites will serve different markets. Taylor will add advanced logic capacity and support research into future manufacturing processes. Austin’s expansion will support fully depleted silicon-on-insulator technology, a process used for specialized chips in industries including aerospace, defense, and automotive. Together, the projects extend Samsung’s U.S. manufacturing footprint from specialty chips to advanced logic for high-performance computing. For Taylor Fab 2, the next milestones are construction, equipment installation, and process qualification before volume production can begin. The 2030 date remains Samsung’s production target.

Sources:

Investment and federal funding. U.S. Commerce Department award announcement
Construction and production timeline. Yonhap reported that Samsung told investors it planned to begin construction by the end of 2026 and was targeting mass production in 2030. Yonhap News Agency

Samsung’s foundry results. Samsung reported growth in high-bandwidth memory base-die sales and discussed its advanced-node and Taylor plans. Samsung’s third-quarter 2026 results
